source.title: Momentum-SAM: Sharpness Aware Minimization without Computational Overhead
source.authors: Marlon Becker; Frederick Altrock; Benjamin Risse

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendix. Some appendix references are garbled (for example, attack names), but this does not affect the extracted findings.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares sharpness measures with generalization-related test performance and reports that lower sharpness does not consistently correspond to better generalization. It does not test the magnitude-aware sharpness measure specified in V7.
record.gate_note: The paper tests Momentum-SAM and compares test accuracy and sharpness across optimizers. Its sharpness measurements are not magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, and it does not report the training–test gap required by V7. Other claim versions are not tested: random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected architecture, adaptive optimizer comparisons under the stated tuning limits, large-batch effects, dropout, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: Appendix A.3.3, Figure A.7 reports test accuracy across batch sizes 64–8192 for WideResNet-16-4 on CIFAR100 over 200 epochs with a constant learning rate. This bears on V5 in a new workload, although the supplied text does not preserve the plotted accuracy curves well enough to determine the outcome. The sharpness analyses do not directly test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that MSAM achieves results comparable to SAM with approximately baseline optimizer runtime and memory use. Their analyses show that its lower measured sharpness does not explain its performance relative to SAM; feature-rank reduction is explored as a complementary explanation, without establishing causality.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces Momentum-SAM, which perturbs in the negative momentum direction, and studies its relation to sharpness and generalization; it does not reproduce the original magnitude-aware sharpness measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: MSAM results vary with perturbation strength, learning-rate scaling, model family, and whether perturbations are applied during ViT warm-up. Applying MSAM during ViT warm-up reduced ViT-S/32 ImageNet test accuracy from 69.1% to 66.1%.

fits_no_version.finding: For WideResNet-16-4 on CIFAR100, MSAM produces lower random filter-normalized loss sharpness and lower Hessian eigenvalues than SAM, without better test accuracy: 79.11±0.09% versus 79.25±0.10%. Filter normalization accounts for weight scale, but these measurements do not establish V7's perturbation tolerance or its relationship with training–test gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lower directional loss sharpness or Hessian curvature need not yield higher test accuracy across sharpness-aware optimizers.

record.problems: The ImageNet optimizer comparisons use single runs for most models; uncertainty is estimated from baseline runs on the smallest models in each category. The sharpness-versus-generalization comparison is presented through figures and textual interpretation rather than a direct quantified training–test-gap analysis.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows were extracted: the sharpness measurements do not use magnitude-scaled perturbations or measure the training–test gap specified by V7. Optimizer test-accuracy results alone do not measure a versioned claim in this catalog.

missing.what: Batch-size sweep reporting test accuracy for batches 64–8192 over 200 epochs with a constant learning rate. Extract the accuracy ordering and values, and establish the optimizer and other fixed settings. The supplied text preserves axes and legends but not readable curves, so neither a batch penalty nor its absence can be established.

record.verdict_notes: The record overlooks the batch-size experiment. No V5 verdict is assigned because its accuracy curves cannot be read from the supplied text. The broader sharpness argument does not justify a T5 verdict on the specific V7 claim.
